title: AWS CloudFormation, CDK and Cost Control: Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on CloudFormation templates, stacks, change sets and drift, CDK synth/deploy, AWS pricing models, Cost Explorer, budgets and the cost traps that inflate bills.

chapters.title: CloudFormation: Templates and Stacks Mental Model
points: A template (JSON/YAML) declares resources; a stack is one deployed instance of it, and CloudFormation creates, updates and deletes resources as a unit
Template sections: Parameters, Mappings, Conditions, Resources (the only required one), Outputs
Intrinsic functions: !Ref (parameter value or resource ID), !GetAtt (resource attribute), !Sub (string substitution), !ImportValue (cross-stack export)
Declarative vs imperative: you state the desired end state and CloudFormation works out the order from Ref/GetAtt dependencies; use DependsOn only for hidden dependencies
Example: minimal YAML template with an S3 bucket (Type: AWS::S3::Bucket) and an Output returning !GetAtt Bucket.Arn

chapters.title: CloudFormation: Change Sets, Drift and Rollback
points: Change set = preview of what an update will add, modify or remove, with a Replacement flag; execute it only after review
Update behaviors: No interruption, Some interruption, Replacement (new physical resource, old one deleted)
Drift detection compares live resources with the template and reports IN_SYNC or DRIFTED; it only detects, it never fixes
Failed create rolls back to ROLLBACK_COMPLETE, which can only be deleted, not updated; failed update rolls back to the last good state
Protect data: DeletionPolicy Retain/Snapshot, UpdateReplacePolicy and stack termination protection; nested stacks and exports split large stacks, and an export in use cannot be changed or deleted

chapters.title: CDK: Constructs, Synth and Deploy
points: CDK defines infrastructure in code (TypeScript, Python and others) and synthesizes it to a CloudFormation template; App contains Stacks which contain Constructs
Construct levels: L1 (Cfn* raw CloudFormation resource), L2 (curated defaults and helpers like bucket.grantRead), L3 (patterns combining several resources)
Core commands: cdk init, cdk synth (emit template to cdk.out), cdk diff (compare with deployed), cdk deploy, cdk destroy
cdk bootstrap is required once per account/region to create the CDKToolkit stack (asset bucket, deploy roles); a missing bootstrap is the usual first deploy failure

CDK vs raw CloudFormation: CDK gives loops, types and reuse but the result is still a CloudFormation stack, so drift and rollback behave the same; unchanged logical IDs keep resources, changing a construct ID causes replacement

chapters.title: AWS Pricing Models and Savings Options
points: On-demand: pay per second/hour with no commitment; the most flexible and most expensive option

Savings Plans: commit to $/hour for 1 or 3 years for up to roughly 70% off; Compute Savings Plans apply across EC2, Fargate and Lambda, EC2 Instance Savings Plans fix family and region for a deeper discount
Reserved Instances: commit to a specific instance configuration; Savings Plans are the more flexible modern default
Spot: spare capacity at up to roughly 90% off, but AWS can reclaim it with a 2-minute warning, so use it only for stateless, fault-tolerant or batch work
Pick by workload: steady baseline gets Savings Plans, spiky or new gets on-demand, interruptible gets Spot; an over-commitment is paid whether used or not

chapters.title: Cost Explorer, Budgets and Cost Traps
points: Cost Explorer: analyze past spend and forecast, grouped by service, account, region or cost allocation tag; tags must be activated in Billing before they appear
AWS Budgets: set a cost, usage, or Savings Plans coverage threshold and alert by email or SNS at actual or forecasted percentages; budget actions can apply IAM or SCP restrictions
Cost Anomaly Detection flags unusual spend automatically, while a budget only fires on a threshold you chose

NAT Gateway trap: you pay an hourly charge plus a per-GB data processing fee on all traffic through it; fix with S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints (free) or interface endpoints, and keep traffic in the same AZ
Other traps: cross-AZ and cross-region data transfer, idle load balancers, unattached EBS volumes and old snapshots, public IPv4 address charges, and CloudWatch Logs retention left at never expire

chapters.title: AWS Cost and IaC Cheat Sheet
points: CloudFormation flow: write template, aws cloudformation create-change-set, review, execute-change-set, then detect-stack-drift
Stack states to know: CREATE_COMPLETE, UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE, ROLLBACK_COMPLETE (delete only), DELETE_FAILED
CDK flow: cdk bootstrap (once), cdk synth, cdk diff, cdk deploy; L1 Cfn*, L2 defaults, L3 patterns
Discounts: Savings Plans up to about 70% for a 1 or 3 year commit, Spot up to about 90% with a 2-minute interruption notice, on-demand has no commitment

Cost checklist: activate cost allocation tags, set a budget with a forecasted alert, enable Anomaly Detection, add S3/DynamoDB gateway endpoints, set log retention, delete idle NAT Gateways, load balancers, EBS volumes and snapshots
